label: Additive hypoglycemic effect
note: Berberine has insulin-sensitising effects similar to metformin. Combined use can cause hypoglycemia, especially in lean or older patients. Monitor fasting glucose if combining.

label: Warfarin antagonism
note: Vitamin K (including K2/MK-7) directly opposes warfarin's anticoagulant effect. Sudden changes in K intake destabilise INR. If on warfarin, keep K intake stable rather than starting/stopping K supplements.

label: Bleeding risk
note: High-dose omega-3 (>3 g/day EPA+DHA) plus warfarin or DOACs increases bleeding risk. Modest doses (1 g/day) appear safer; clinical guidance is to use the lowest effective dose.

label: Bleeding risk
note: Ginkgo's PAF antagonism plus warfarin's anticoagulation has caused major bleeding events. Avoid combination unless specifically cleared by clinician.

label: Duplicate therapy
note: Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, chemically identical to lovastatin. Combining with prescription statins doubles dose and rhabdomyolysis risk. Pick one or the other.

label: CYP3A4 inhibition
note: Grapefruit (and grapefruit juice) inhibits CYP3A4, raising blood levels of simvastatin, lovastatin, and atorvastatin. Increases myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk. Pravastatin and rosuvastatin are largely unaffected.

label: Serotonin syndrome
note: St. John's Wort has SSRI-like effects. Combined with prescription SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs it can precipitate serotonin syndrome. Do not combine.

label: Hypertensive crisis
note: Aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented soy, draft beer have high tyramine; with MAOIs this can trigger hypertensive crisis. Strict diet required.

label: Lithium toxicity
note: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance and can raise serum lithium 25–60%. If chronic NSAID use is unavoidable, lithium dose may need reduction; check levels.

label: Lithium toxicity
note: ACE inhibitors and ARBs can elevate serum lithium. Recheck levels 5–7 days after initiating either drug class.

label: Reduced absorption
note: Calcium (and iron) bind levothyroxine in the gut, reducing absorption ~25%. Separate doses by at least 4 hours.

label: Reduced absorption
note: Iron salts reduce levothyroxine absorption substantially. Take at least 4 hours apart.

label: Reduced absorption
note: Calcium (and any divalent cation) blocks oral bisphosphonate absorption. Take bisphosphonate first thing AM with plain water; wait 30–60 min before food, calcium, or other meds.

label: Hyperkalemia
note: Spironolactone, eplerenone, amiloride raise potassium. Adding potassium supplements or salt substitutes (KCl) can cause dangerous hyperkalemia. Avoid the combo unless monitored.

label: Volume depletion
note: Both deplete intravascular volume. Combined use raises hypotension and AKI risk. Hold one during acute illness or dehydration ('sick-day rules').

label: Respiratory depression
note: Both are CNS depressants; combined use markedly raises overdose and death risk, especially in elderly. Avoid.

label: Respiratory depression
note: FDA black-box warning. Combined use multiplies overdose risk. Avoid; if both unavoidable, lowest effective doses with naloxone access.

label: Reduced digoxin levels
note: St. John's Wort induces P-glycoprotein, lowering digoxin AUC ~25%, risking treatment failure in heart failure or AF.

label: Bone marrow toxicity
note: Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, the major route of azathioprine clearance. Azathioprine dose must be reduced ~75% if combined; better to avoid.

label: Reduced absorption
note: Cipro/levofloxacin chelate with divalent cations (Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn) → loss of oral bioavailability. Separate doses by 2 hours before / 6 hours after.

label: Reduced absorption
note: Same divalent-cation chelation problem. Take tetracycline 1 h before food/dairy/calcium supplements.

label: Serotonin syndrome
note: Concurrent or rapid switch between MAOI and SSRI risks serotonin syndrome. Wash-out 14 days minimum.

label: Hyperkalemia
note: ACE inhibitors raise potassium retention. Adding K supplements or salt substitutes can cause hyperkalemia, particularly in CKD.

label: Cardio-protection blunted
note: Ibuprofen taken before aspirin can prevent the irreversible COX-1 binding aspirin needs for cardioprotection. Take aspirin first; or use naproxen/celecoxib.

label: Reduced non-heme iron absorption
note: Coffee/tea polyphenols inhibit non-heme iron absorption ~40–60% when taken with the meal. Drink them ≥1 h after iron-rich meals if iron-deficient.

label: Copper depletion
note: Chronic zinc >40 mg/day depletes copper, causing anemia and neuropathy. If supplementing zinc long-term, include 1–2 mg copper or get tested.

label: Raised amiodarone levels
note: CYP3A4 inhibition raises amiodarone exposure → torsades, bradycardia. Avoid grapefruit while on amiodarone.

label: Hypotension
note: Grapefruit raises felodipine/nifedipine/amlodipine plasma levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, risking hypotension. Avoid grapefruit on these meds.

label: Reduced antiplatelet effect
note: Omeprazole and esomeprazole inhibit CYP2C19, the enzyme that activates clopidogrel. Pantoprazole or famotidine are safer alternatives.

label: Reduced absorption
note: Large amino-acid loads compete with levodopa for transport across gut and BBB. Time levodopa 30+ minutes before protein-rich meals to keep on-time stable.
